title: sylvester-gallai-theorem-oq-01: every finite non-collinear point set has an ordinary line

problemStatement.formal: For a finite S : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) with ¬ Collinear ℝ (↑S), there exist a b ∈ S, a ≠ b, such that the connecting line line[ℝ, a, b] is ordinary: ∀ c ∈ S, Collinear ℝ {a, b, c} → c = a ∨ c = b.
problemStatement.plain: Sylvester–Gallai theorem: given finitely many points in the plane that do not all lie on one line, there is always a line that passes through exactly two of the points (an 'ordinary line'). Equivalently: it is impossible to arrange finitely many points, not all collinear, so that every line through two of them passes through a third.
whyMatters: Foundational result of combinatorial / incidence geometry; posed by Sylvester (1893), first proved by Melchior (1940) and independently Gallai; Kelly's metric proof (1948) is the canonical elementary argument.
Gateway to the de Bruijn–Erdős theorem, the Motzkin–Hansen bounds, the Green–Tao 'ordinary lines' theorem, and the orchard-planting problem.
Not present in Mathlib — a genuine formalization gap. Confirmed by source search: no `SylvesterGallai`, `ordinaryLine`, or de Bruijn–Erdős declarations exist.

proven: Melchior 1940 (dual, via Euler's formula on the arrangement of lines).
Kelly 1948 (metric/minimal-distance proof — the route chosen here).
All required Mathlib primitives exist (collinearity, orthogonal projection, distance-to-affine-subspace, betweenness, finite-min).

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: sylvester-gallai-theorem-oq-01

**Goal.** Formalize the Sylvester–Gallai theorem in Lean 4 / Mathlib: *every finite set of points in the Euclidean plane, not all collinear, determines an ordinary line* (a line through exactly two of the points).

---

## Session 1 (researcher-8, 2026-06-18) — OBSERVE → ORIENT (build-free)

Build host saturated (≥6 lean-build containers on a 7.65 GiB Docker VM → OOM). This session is a **build-free ORIENT**: confirm the gap, fix the architecture, map to Mathlib, size the work. No Lean code committed.

### Mathlib gap — confirmed

Exhaustive source grep of `proofs/.lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/`: **no** `SylvesterGallai`, `ordinaryLine`, `OrdinaryLine`, or de Bruijn–Erdős declarations. The theorem is a genuine contribution. (The only `Erdős–Szekeres` hit is the monotone-subsequence theorem in `Order.OrderIsoNat`, unrelated.)

### Why Kelly, not Melchior

Two classical proofs:
- **Melchior (1940), dual:** apply Euler's formula `V − E + F = 2` to the arrangement of the dual lines; a counting argument forces an ordinary point. Needs planar-arrangement / Euler-characteristic infrastructure Mathlib lacks.
- **Kelly (1948), metric:** minimize point-to-line distance; the minimizing line is ordinary. Needs only orthogonal projection, distance, betweenness, and a finite minimum — **all in Mathlib**. This is the chosen route.

### Statement (target)

```lean
theorem sylvester_gallai
    (S : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    (hS : ¬ Collinear ℝ (↑S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))) :
    ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧
      ∀ c ∈ S, Collinear ℝ ({a, b, c} : Set _) → c = a ∨ c = b
```
The conclusion says the connecting line `line[ℝ, a, b]` is **ordinary**: any third point of `S` collinear with `a,b` is already `a` or `b`. (Working in `Fin 2` keeps the cross-product distance formula 1-dimensional; a general inner-product-space version can come later.)

### Kelly's proof, decomposed into Lean lemmas

Let `dline x a b := dist x (line[ℝ,a,b])` (distance from `x` to the line through `a,b`).

**Lemma B — minimization domain nonempty.** From `¬ Collinear` there are distinct `a,b ∈ S`; if every `c ∈ S` lay on `line[a,b]` then `S` would be collinear, so some `P ∈ S` has `P ∉ line[a,b]`, giving a triple with `dline P a b > 0`.

**Lemma C — minimizer exists.** The set of triples `T = {(P,a,b) ∈ S³ : a≠b, P ∉ line[a,b]}` is finite (`Finset` product) and (by B) nonempty, so `Finset.exists_min_image` yields a minimizer `(P₀,a₀,b₀)` with `δ := dline P₀ a₀ b₀ > 0` minimal. Let `ℓ₀ := line[ℝ,a₀,b₀]`.

**Lemma D — the minimizing line is ordinary (the hard kernel).** Suppose `ℓ₀` contains ≥3 points of `S`. Let `F := orthogonalProjection (affineSpan ℝ {a₀,b₀}) P₀` (foot of perpendicular); `dist P₀ F = δ`.
  - *Pigeonhole (same side of foot).* Parametrize `ℓ₀` about `F`: by `collinear_iff_of_mem` each on-line point `= r • v +ᵥ F` for some `r : ℝ`. The **sign** of `r` is the side of `F`. Among ≥3 points, two share a sign (pigeonhole on `{<0, ≥0}` etc.); distinct same-side points have distinct `|r|`. Take `B` (smaller `|r|`, nearer `F`) and `C` (larger). Then `FB < FC`, `B ≠ C`.
  - *Non-degeneracy.* `P₀ ∉ ℓ₀`, `B,C ∈ ℓ₀` ⟹ `line[P₀,C] ∩ ℓ₀ = {C}` ⟹ `B ∉ line[P₀,C]` (else `B=C`). Also `B,C ≠ P₀`. Hence `(B,P₀,C) ∈ T`.
  - *Distance strictly decreases.* In the right triangle `P₀ F C` (right angle at `F`), drop perpendicular `B → line[P₀,C]`, foot `G`. Triangles `C G B ∼ C F P₀` (right angles, shared angle at `C`), so
    `dist B (line[P₀,C]) = BG = P₀F · (CB / CP₀) = δ · (CB / CP₀)`.
    Since `CB ≤ CF < CP₀` (leg `<` hypotenuse, because `FP₀ = δ > 0`), the ratio `CB/CP₀ < 1`, so `dist B (line[P₀,C]) < δ`. (Includes `B = F`: then it is the altitude-to-hypotenuse length `P₀F·FC/P₀C < δ`.)
  - *Contradiction.* `(B,P₀,C) ∈ T` with `dline B P₀ C < δ` contradicts minimality of `δ`. So `ℓ₀` has exactly 2 points of `S` ⟹ `a₀,b₀` is the ordinary pair. ∎

### Mathlib API map (from source reconnaissance)

| Need | Declaration | Module |
|------|-------------|--------|
| Collinearity | `Collinear ℝ s`, `collinear_iff_of_mem`, `collinear_pair`, `affineIndependent_iff_not_collinear_set` | `LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/FiniteDimensional` |
| Line through 2 pts | `line[ℝ, a, b]` = `affineSpan ℝ {a,b}`, `left_mem_affineSpan_pair`, `right_mem_affineSpan_pair` | `LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/AffineSubspace/Defs` |
| Foot of perpendicular | `EuclideanGeometry.orthogonalProjection`, `orthogonalProjection_mem`, `vsub_orthogonalProjection_mem_direction_orthogonal` | `Geometry/Euclidean/Projection` |
| Distance to line | `dist_orthogonalProjection_eq_infDist`, `dist_sq_eq_dist_orthogonalProjection_sq_add_dist_orthogonalProjection_sq` (Pythagoras) | `Geometry/Euclidean/Projection` |
| Finite minimum | `Finset.exists_min_image` | `Data/Finset/Max` |
| Betweenness | `Wbtw`, `Sbtw`, `affineSegment_subset_affineSpan` | `Analysis/Convex/Between` |

### Infrastructure assessment

- **Cross-product distance formula** `dist x line[a,b] = |det[b-a, x-a]| / ‖b-a‖` in `Fin 2`: not packaged; derive from `orthogonalProjection` or `Matrix.det`/area. ~30-60 lines. This is the lever that turns Lemma D's inequality into an algebraic `CB/CP₀ < 1`.
- **Same-side-of-foot pigeonhole**: not packaged; build from `collinear_iff_of_mem` + sign trichotomy. ~40-80 lines.
- **Lemma D assembly**: the similar-triangles / leg-ratio inequality. ~100-200 lines (the crux).
- **Lemmas B, C + glue**: ~100-150 lines (routine).
- **Total estimate: 500–900 lines, multi-session.** Decision: **BUILD** (no elementary shortcut for the full theorem; `tractability 4` is accurate — doable but the geometric kernel is delicate). Lemmas B, C and the distance formula are good independent **Aristotle** candidates once statements are fixed.

### Dead ends / cautions

- Do **not** pursue Melchior's dual proof — the planar-arrangement Euler-characteristic machinery is a much larger Mathlib gap than Kelly's metric primitives.
- Avoid stating in a general `InnerProductSpace` first: the cross-product distance lever is cleanest in `Fin 2`; generalize only after the `Fin 2` proof closes.
- Build host is OOM-prone; keep the file **standalone + unregistered** while iterating, build single-target via the Docker wrapper only when `lean-build` container count is 0.


---

## Session 2 (researcher-1, 2026-06-18) — REDIRECT: reduce to the verified gallery proof (build-free)

**Discovery.** Sylvester–Gallai is *already* fully verified in this repository: `Proofs/Erdos606OQ03OQ03.lean`, namespace `SylvesterGallai`, theorem `sylvester_gallai` (`508` lines, **0 sorries, 0 axioms**, registered in `Proofs.lean`). It is Kelly's proof, stated over `Point := ℝ × ℝ` with a cross-product collinearity predicate `SylvesterGallai.Collinear a b c := ∃ t, c.1-a.1 = t*(b.1-a.1) ∧ c.2-a.2 = t*(b.2-a.2)`.

**Consequence.** The Session-1 plan (re-derive Kelly's 6-case kernel over `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, est. 500–900 lines) is *unnecessary*. The canonical-Mathlib-types statement follows by a **reduction** along the coordinate map `φ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ × ℝ`, `φ x = (x 0, x 1)`.

**File authored:** `Proofs/SylvesterGallaiOQ01.lean` (standalone, unregistered, fleet-safe). It states

```lean
theorem sylvester_gallai (S : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    (hS : ¬ Collinear ℝ (↑S : Set _)) :
    ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ IsOrdinary S a b
```

and proves it by: transport `S ↦ S.image φ`, invoke `SylvesterGallai.sylvester_gallai`, pull the ordinary pair back through `φ` (injective). The full reduction glue is written; **4 mechanical bridge lemmas remain as `sorry`**:

| Lemma | Content | Mathlib lever |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| `phi_injective` | `φ` injective | `Fin 2` funext |
| `three_le_card_of_not_collinear` | `¬Collinear ↑S → 3 ≤ S.card` | `Set.Subsingleton.collinear`, `collinear_pair` |
| `collinear_iff_sg` (a≠b) | `Collinear ℝ {a,b,c} ↔ SG.Collinear (φa)(φb)(φc)` | `collinear_iff_of_mem` + `Fin 2` coords |
| `not_allCollinear_image` | `¬Collinear ↑S → ¬AllCollinear (S.image φ)` | contrapositive of the above + injectivity |

**Key subtlety.** The custom predicate equals Mathlib's `Collinear ℝ {a,b,c}` only when `a ≠ b` (at `a=b` the custom form forces `c=a`, Mathlib's is vacuous), hence `collinear_iff_sg` carries `a ≠ b` — always available in the ordinary-line context. Only the *forward* map `φ` is needed (no inverse), avoiding the fiddly `PiLp`/`EuclideanSpace` element construction.

**Status:** `formalized` (reduction written, bridge lemmas `sorry`, build-pending — host saturated). The geometric content is closed; what remains is bookkeeping along an isomorphism.
